title: A Dangerous Invitation
content:
For the next three days, Lila and Darius developed a routine neither was willing to acknowledge.

He appeared while she watered her plants. She found reasons to walk past his driveway. He sent her a message asking whether she knew a good grocery store, despite having already discovered one less than a mile away.

On Thursday evening, he knocked on her door carrying two takeaway bags.

“Dinner,” he announced.

Lila peered into the bags. “You bought food?”

“I was afraid you'd make me survive on bottled water again.”

“Smart man.”

He stepped inside, and she noticed the difference immediately. The first evening had been an accident of convenience. This time, he had come because he wanted to see her.

That realization made her nervous.

They ate on the sofa, arguing about movies and trading embarrassing stories. Darius was easier to talk to than she had expected. Beneath his confident exterior was a thoughtful man who listened carefully and remembered small details.

He remembered that she hated thunderstorms.

He remembered that she took her coffee without sugar.

And he remembered that she had once mentioned wanting to learn salsa dancing.

“You're staring,” Lila said when she caught him watching her.

“I'm thinking.”

“Dangerous habit.”

“I'm thinking that I should have asked you out properly instead of pretending I needed help finding groceries.”

She set down her fork.

“You mean this isn't about the groceries?”

“Not even slightly.”

His honesty left her with no clever response.

Darius leaned back, giving her room to decide how she wanted to answer.

“There's a restaurant downtown I've wanted to try,” he continued. “Saturday night. Dinner with me?”

Lila pretended to consider it.

“Will there be food?”

“An unreasonable amount.”

“Good conversation?”

“I'll do my best.”

“And what exactly are you expecting in return?”

His expression turned serious.

“Nothing you don't want to give.”

The answer surprised her. She had expected another joke, another flirtatious challenge. Instead, he had made it clear that the choice was hers.

She smiled.

“Saturday. Eight o'clock.”

His face brightened.

“Wear something that makes you feel beautiful.”

“Planning to impress me, Mr. Kane?”

“Planning to try.”

Saturday arrived with a sky full of threatening clouds.

Lila spent nearly an hour deciding what to wear before settling on a fitted burgundy dress that made her feel elegant, confident, and just a little dangerous.

When she stepped onto her porch, Darius was waiting beside his car.

For the first time since meeting him, he seemed momentarily lost for words.

Lila glanced down at herself.

“Something wrong?”

“No.”

He shook his head, smiling.

“I'm trying to decide whether I should compliment the dress or admit that I'm going to spend the entire evening trying not to stare at you.”

Her cheeks warmed.

“Compliment the dress. We'll discuss the staring later.”

“Beautiful dress,” he said. “Beautiful woman wearing it.”

She slipped her hand into his offered arm.

“Better.”

The restaurant was intimate, with candlelit tables and soft music. Their conversation flowed so easily that Lila barely noticed the time passing.

Darius told her about the pressure he had felt to succeed in the city. Lila admitted that her last relationship had ended because she had spent too long trying to become the woman someone else wanted.

“I don't want to do that again,” she said.

“Then don't.”

“It's not always that simple.”

“No,” he agreed. “But you shouldn't have to shrink yourself to keep someone interested.”

She studied him, wondering how a man she had known for less than a week could say something that felt so personal.

When dinner ended, neither suggested going home.

They walked beneath the restaurant awning as the first drops of rain began to fall.

Darius offered his jacket.

Lila shook her head. “You'll get wet.”

“I'll survive.”

She moved closer beneath the awning.

“You're annoyingly considerate.”

“Is that a compliment?”

“Don't push your luck.”

He laughed, then grew quiet as he looked at her.

“Can I kiss you?”

The question sent a small thrill through her.

She had been waiting for him to ask all evening.

“Yes.”

He touched her cheek, giving her time to change her mind, then kissed her gently.

It was nothing like the dramatic kisses in her favorite movies. It was warmer, slower, and somehow more dangerous because it felt so natural.

When they parted, Lila was smiling.

“That was a decent first attempt.”

“Decent?”

“You'll have to work on your technique.”

Darius laughed, then leaned closer.

“Challenge accepted.”

The second kiss lasted longer.

When he finally drove her home, they sat outside her house with the engine switched off, neither wanting to end the evening.

“Come inside,” Lila said at last.

Darius turned toward her.

“Are you sure?”

She nodded, her expression suddenly shy.

“I'd like you to stay a little longer.”

He took her hand.

“Then I'd love to.”

Inside, they stood together in the quiet hallway, close enough that Lila could feel the warmth of his presence.

For once, she didn't have a joke ready.

Darius brushed a strand of hair away from her face.

“Tell me if you want me to slow down.”

“I will.”

She reached for him, and their lips met again.

Outside, the rain grew heavier.

Inside, Lila stopped thinking about tomorrow.

For the first time in months, she allowed herself to want something without immediately searching for a reason to fear it.
